brief: Nomura's McElligott says the VIX floor has moved up from 15-16 to 18 (VVIX from 80-90s to mid-90s) because realized VVIX volatility just hit a 10-year record, signaling a regime shift that holds until the market's spinning plates clear, with the Anthropic IPO his top candidate. He argues this cannot become a vol squeeze because negative gamma is absent: leveraged VIX ETN positioning is barely net long after holders redeemed into last week's selloff (Korean retail was the main source, and Korean equities are still falling), and VIX options dealers are long gamma, with call demand low and deep out-of-the-money. A 10-point VIX jump would now force only a fraction of the vega buying it once did, unlike 2018's Volmageddon, when forced ETN buying turned a selloff into a crash. Spot-vol correlation is reverting to normal, but McElligott says Asian exotics hedging flow, which buys vol as spot rises and sells as it falls, works against that. Goldman's desk instead favors downside skew. Levered ETFs face a record buy into today's close. Zero Hedge adds that stock-forced flows are bigger than ever even as vol-forcing flows drain, so the next selloff may not show up in the VIX at all.
